title: apps/alerting/rules — subsystem map (App-SDK app for AlertRule/RecordingRule/RuleSequence/Config)
answers: Where is admission validation/mutation for alert rules handled?
How does control flow into apps/alerting/rules from the rest of Grafana?
What does apps/alerting/rules own vs not own?
body:
apps/alerting/rules is a Grafana App-SDK app implementing k8s API group `rules.alerting.grafana.app/v0alpha1` with kinds AlertRule, RecordingRule, RuleSequence, Config. It only does schema (CUE), mutation/defaulting, and admission validation — rule evaluation/storage lives in pkg/services/ngalert/.
- Entry point: `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/app.go:New` builds a `simple.AppManagedKind` per kind (from `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/apis/types.go:GetKinds`) via `buildKindValidator`/`buildKindMutator`/`buildKindWatcher`.
- External wiring: `pkg/registry/apps/alerting/rules/register.go:RegisterAppInstaller` supplies the real `config.RuntimeConfig` (`apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/config/runtime.go`) — FolderValidator, NotificationSettingsValidator, ResolveRuleRef, MembershipResolver, search handlers — backed by ngalert/folder service/unified storage. Inside the app dir, RuntimeConfig is just an interface boundary.
- Admission: `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/validation/builder.go:Builder.Build` fans out per-action ValidateFuncs (`OnWrite`/`OnDelete`/`WithOpenAPIValidation`); mutators (e.g. `alertrule/mutator.go:NewMutator`) run first. Delete requests only populate `req.OldObject`, not `req.Object` (handled explicitly in `Builder.Build`'s switch).
- RuleSequence state: `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/rulesequence/membership_index.go:MembershipIndex` is an in-memory watch-backed index kept in sync by app-sdk's informer calling Add/Update/Delete; before initial sync it is empty and Resolve returns not-found (intentionally permissive).
- Search routes are wired via `kinds/searchRoutes.cue` + `apps/alerting/rules/pkg/app/search_routes_test.go:buildSearchRoutes`, served through `config.RuntimeConfig.SearchRulesHandler`/`SearchAlertRulesHandler`/`SearchRecordingRulesHandler`.
- Tests are pure unit tests with hand-built RuntimeConfig fakes (`app_test.go`), no server/DB: run `go test ./apps/alerting/rules/...`.
